```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the get-started vignette: the
# source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a bare
# installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`ms_tally()` turns variant records into **mutation catalogs** — sample ×
channel count matrices on the community channel schemas. This guide walks
the tally for SBS and DBS against a reference genome, shows the schema
family, and closes with hypermutant stratification. Bringing variants in is
covered by [Importing variant data](import-data.html); the extraction step
that consumes catalogs is [Extracting signatures](signature-extraction.html).

## A genome to tally against

The tally needs the reference genome around each variant to place
mutations in their trinucleotide (and transcriptional) context. msuiter
reads the 2bit format directly — point `ms_tally()` at a `.2bit` file for
the build your variants were called against (for example the UCSC or
Ensembl 2bit download for GRCh38).

For a fully offline guide, build a miniature two-chromosome 2bit with the
same writer the package's own executable tour uses, and place variants on
it:

```{r genome, cache = FALSE}
.u32le <- function(x) writeBin(as.integer(x), raw(), size = 4L, endian = "little")
.pack_bases <- function(ints) {
  code <- c(A = 0L, C = 1L, G = 2L, T = 3L)
  bases <- code[match(ints, c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L))]
  bases[is.na(bases)] <- 0L
  out <- raw((length(bases) + 3L) %/% 4L)
  acc <- 0L; filled <- 0L; k <- 0L
  for (b in bases) {
    acc <- bitwOr(bitwShiftL(acc, 2L), b); filled <- filled + 1L
    if (filled == 4L) { k <- k + 1L; out[k] <- as.raw(acc); acc <- 0L; filled <- 0L }
  }
  if (filled > 0L) out[k + 1L] <- as.raw(bitwShiftL(acc, 2L * (4L - filled)))
  out
}
.write_2bit <- function(path) {
  chr1 <- rep(c(2L, 1L), 32L)
  chr2 <- rep(c(3L, 1L), 20L)
  recs <- list(
    list(name = "chr1", size = 64L, dna = .pack_bases(chr1),
         nb = integer(0), nl = integer(0)),
    list(name = "chr2", size = 40L, dna = .pack_bases(chr2),
         nb = integer(0), nl = integer(0)))
  off <- 16L + sum(vapply(recs, function(r) 1L + nchar(r$name) + 4L, 0L))
  index <- raw(); body <- raw()
  for (r in recs) {
    index <- c(index, as.raw(nchar(r$name)), charToRaw(r$name), .u32le(off))
    rec <- c(.u32le(r$size), .u32le(length(r$nb)), .u32le(r$nb), .u32le(r$nl),
             .u32le(0L), .u32le(0L), r$dna)
    body <- c(body, rec); off <- off + length(rec)
  }
  bytes <- c(.u32le(0x1A412743L), .u32le(0L), .u32le(length(recs)),
             .u32le(0L), index, body)
  con <- file(path, "wb"); on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  writeBin(bytes, con); invisible(path)
}
genome <- file.path(tempdir(), "catalogs-2bit.2bit")
.write_2bit(genome)
```

Replace this file with a real 2bit in your own analysis — the rest of the
grammar is unchanged.

## The SBS tally

```{r variants}
tab <- data.frame(
  chrom  = c("chr1", "chr1", "chr1", "chr2", "chr2", "chr1"),
  start  = c(12L, 22L, 14L, 9L, 31L, 50L),
  end    = c(12L, 22L, 14L, 9L, 31L, 50L),
  ref    = c("C", "C", "C", "T", "T", "G"),
  alt    = c("A", "T", "T", "A", "C", "T"),
  sample = c("S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3"))
v <- ms_variants(tab, "GRCh38", caller = "catalogs-guide",
                 matched_normal = "none")
cat96 <- ms_tally(v, genome, mode = "SBS96")
cat96
```

The result is an `MsCatalog`: the sample × channel matrix plus a validated
channel-table record (name and content hash) that every downstream step —
extraction, fitting, comparison, export — pins its semantics to.

```{r inspect}
cnt <- cat96@counts
dim(cnt)                      # channels x samples
head(cnt[1L:4L, ])            # the first four channels
cat96@channels$name
```

## The schema family

`mode` selects the channel schema. The substitution family spans the
96-channel canonical schema, the transcriptionally stranded 192, the
stranded-with-mutational-signature 384, and the full 1536 expansion; DBS
variants tally to 78 channels:

```{r modes}
cat78 <- ms_tally(v, genome, mode = "DBS78")
cat78@channels$name
dim(cat78@counts)
```

The schema registry is versioned and content-hashed; importing or exporting
a catalog whose labels do not ride the registry is rejected at the boundary
(see [Importing variant data](import-data.html)).

MNV calls and complex substitutions do not fold silently into SBS/DBS
channels: they are routed to their own ledger and skipped, so a catalog is
always an honest accounting of what the tallier saw.

## Stratifying hypermutants

Tumors with extreme mutation burden can dominate an analysis. The
stratifier assigns samples to a hypermutant class (data-driven by default,
or with a manual cutoff) so you can fit or describe the two arms separately:

```{r stratify}
strat <- ms_stratify_hypermutants(cat96, seed = 1)
strat
```
